chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Whoever practices medicine or veterinary treatment, let him obtain indemnity from his guardian; otherwise, he is liable for him.”

key_terms.الْبَرَاءَةَ: prior release from liability or indemnity
key_terms.تَبَيْطَرَ: undertook the treatment of animals as a veterinarian
key_terms.ضَامِنٌ: legally liable or responsible for compensation
key_terms.وَلِيِّهِ: his guardian or legal authority responsible for him

ai.seo_question: Is a physician or veterinarian legally liable if treatment causes harm without prior indemnity?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning liability in treatment. It establishes that one who undertakes medical or veterinary practice must obtain prior indemnity from the relevant guardian, otherwise he bears legal responsibility for resulting harm.
